java.lang.String: The String class represents character strings in Java. All string literals are implemented as instances of this class. Strings are constant (immutable); their values cannot be changed after creation. The class provides methods for examining characters, comparing strings, searching, extracting substrings, and case conversions.
java.lang.String.valueOf: Returns the string representation of the argument. Multiple overloads exist for different types (Object, char[], boolean, char, int, long, float, double). For objects, returns 'null' if the argument is null, otherwise returns obj.toString().
java.lang.System: The System class contains useful class fields and methods. It cannot be instantiated. Provides access to standard input/output/error streams, system properties, environment variables, and utility methods for array copying and time.
java.lang.System.arraycopy: Copies an array from a source array to a destination array. Parameters: src (source array), srcPos (starting position in source), dest (destination array), destPos (starting position in destination), length (number of elements to copy).
java.lang.System.currentTimeMillis: Returns the current time in milliseconds since January 1, 1970 UTC (Unix epoch). The granularity depends on the operating system and may be coarser than one millisecond.
java.lang.System.getProperty: Gets the system property indicated by the specified key. Returns null if the property doesn't exist. Common properties include 'user.dir', 'java.home', 'os.name', etc.
java.lang.System.println: Prints a message to the standard output stream followed by a line separator. This is typically accessed via System.out.println().
java.lang.System.split: Note: This is not a System method. String.split() splits a string around matches of a regular expression.
java.lang.Math: The Math class contains methods for performing basic numeric operations such as exponential, logarithm, square root, and trigonometric functions. All methods are static.
java.lang.Math.abs: Returns the absolute value of a value. Overloaded for int, long, float, and double. Note: Integer.MIN_VALUE and Long.MIN_VALUE return unchanged (negative) due to overflow.
java.lang.Math.min: Returns the smaller of two values. Overloaded for int, long, float, and double. For floating-point, treats -0 as strictly smaller than +0 and returns NaN if either argument is NaN.
java.lang.Math.max: Returns the larger of two values. Overloaded for int, long, float, and double. For floating-point, treats -0 as strictly smaller than +0 and returns NaN if either argument is NaN.
java.lang.Integer: The Integer class wraps a primitive int value in an object. Provides conversion methods between int and String, plus utility constants and methods for integer manipulation.
java.lang.Integer.MAX_VALUE: A constant representing the maximum value an int can hold: 2^31 - 1 (2,147,483,647).
java.lang.Integer.toHexString: Returns a string representation of the integer argument as an unsigned integer in base 16. Uses characters 0-9 and a-f, with no leading zeros.
java.lang.Long: The Long class wraps a primitive long value in an object. Provides conversion methods between long and String, plus utility constants for working with 64-bit signed integers.
java.lang.Long.MIN_VALUE: A constant representing the minimum value a long can hold: -2^63 (-9,223,372,036,854,775,808).
java.lang.Long.parseLong: Parses the string argument as a signed decimal long. Throws NumberFormatException if the string cannot be parsed. An overloaded version accepts a radix parameter.
java.lang.Double: The Double class wraps a primitive double value in an object. Provides conversion methods, special value constants (NaN, POSITIVE_INFINITY), and comparison utilities.
java.lang.Double.compare: Compares two double values numerically. Returns a negative value if d1 < d2, zero if equal, positive if d1 > d2. Handles special cases like NaN correctly.
java.lang.Boolean: The Boolean class wraps a primitive boolean value in an object. Provides conversion methods between boolean and String.
java.lang.Boolean.TRUE: A static final Boolean instance representing the primitive value true.
java.lang.Boolean.FALSE: A static final Boolean instance representing the primitive value false.
java.lang.Character: The Character class wraps a primitive char value in an object. Provides methods for determining character categories (letter, digit, whitespace) and converting cases based on Unicode.
java.lang.Character.MAX_VALUE: A constant representing the largest value of type char: '\uFFFF' (65,535).
java.lang.Character.isDigit: Determines if the specified character is a digit (0-9). Returns true for Unicode decimal digits.
java.lang.Character.isWhitespace: Determines if the specified character is white space according to Java's definition. Includes space, tab, newline, and other whitespace characters.
java.lang.Character.toUpperCase: Converts the character argument to uppercase using Unicode case mapping rules.
java.lang.StringBuilder: A mutable sequence of characters. Provides an API compatible with StringBuffer but without synchronization. Designed for use by a single thread, making it faster than StringBuffer.
java.lang.StringBuffer: A thread-safe, mutable sequence of characters. Similar to String but allows modification. Methods are synchronized for multi-threaded use. For single-threaded use, StringBuilder is preferred.
java.lang.Class: Instances of Class represent classes and interfaces in a running Java application. Created automatically by the JVM when loading classes. Provides reflection capabilities.
java.lang.Class.forName: Returns the Class object associated with the class or interface with the given string name. The class is initialized if not already. Throws ClassNotFoundException if not found.
java.lang.Object: The root of the Java class hierarchy. Every class has Object as a superclass. Provides fundamental methods like equals(), hashCode(), toString(), and wait()/notify().
java.lang.Throwable: The superclass of all errors and exceptions in Java. Only objects of this class or its subclasses can be thrown by the JVM or the throw statement. Provides stack trace and exception chaining.
java.lang.Thread.loadClass: Note: loadClass() is a ClassLoader method, not Thread. It loads a class with the specified name, returning the Class object.
java.lang.reflect.Array: The Array class provides static methods to dynamically create and access Java arrays. Supports get/set operations with automatic widening conversions.
java.lang.reflect.Array.getLength: Returns the length of the specified array object as an int. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the argument is not an array.
java.lang.reflect.Array.newInstance: Creates a new array with the specified component type and dimensions. Throws NegativeArraySizeException for negative dimensions.
java.lang.reflect.Type: The common superinterface for all types in Java, including raw types, parameterized types, array types, type variables, and primitive types.
java.lang.reflect.ParameterizedType: Represents a parameterized type such as Collection<String>. Provides methods to get actual type arguments, raw type, and owner type.
java.lang.reflect.TypeVariable: Represents a type variable declared on a generic class, interface, method, or constructor. Provides access to bounds and the declaring element.
java.util.Arrays: Contains static methods for manipulating arrays (sorting, searching, comparing, filling). Also provides methods to view arrays as lists.
java.util.Arrays.asList: Returns a fixed-size list backed by the specified array. Changes to the array are reflected in the list and vice versa. The list does not support add/remove operations.
java.util.Arrays.binarySearch: Searches the specified sorted array for the specified value using binary search. The array must be sorted before calling this method.
java.util.Arrays.collect: Note: collect() is a Stream method, not Arrays. Use Arrays.stream().collect() to collect array elements.
java.util.Arrays.equals: Returns true if two arrays are equal - same length and corresponding elements are equal.
java.util.ArrayList: Resizable-array implementation of the List interface. Permits all elements including null. Provides constant-time get/set operations and amortized constant-time add.
java.util.HashMap: Hash table-based implementation of the Map interface. Permits null keys and values. Provides constant-time performance for get/put with proper hash distribution.
java.util.List: An ordered collection (sequence) that provides precise control over element insertion positions and integer index-based access. Typically allows duplicates.
java.util.Map: An object that maps keys to values. Cannot contain duplicate keys; each key maps to at most one value. Replaces the legacy Dictionary class.
java.util.Collection: The root interface in the collection hierarchy. Represents a group of objects (elements). Provides basic operations like add, remove, contains, size, and iteration.
java.util.Iterator: An iterator over a collection. Provides methods to traverse elements (hasNext, next) and optionally remove elements during iteration.
java.util.Collections: Consists exclusively of static methods that operate on or return collections. Provides algorithms (sort, search), wrappers (synchronized, unmodifiable), and utility methods.
java.util.Collections.emptyList: Returns an empty immutable list. This list is serializable and its iterator handles remove() correctly.
java.util.Stack: A last-in-first-out (LIFO) stack of objects extending Vector. Provides push, pop, peek, empty, and search operations. Deque implementations are preferred for modern code.
java.util.Vector: A synchronized growable array implementation. Thread-safe but slower than ArrayList. For non-threaded applications, ArrayList is recommended.
java.util.Properties: Represents a persistent set of properties (key-value string pairs). Can be saved to or loaded from a stream. Supports default values via a chained Properties object.
java.util.Enumeration: An object that generates a series of elements sequentially. Legacy interface; Iterator is preferred for new implementations.
java.util.WeakHashMap: A hash table-based Map implementation with weak keys. Entries are automatically removed when their keys are no longer in ordinary use (garbage collected).
java.util.Locale: Represents a specific geographical, political, or cultural region. Used for locale-sensitive operations like number/date formatting.
java.util.Locale.ENGLISH: A static Locale constant representing the English language.
java.util.regex.Matcher: An engine that performs match operations on a character sequence by interpreting a Pattern. Supports matches(), lookingAt(), and find() operations.
java.util.regex.MatchResult: The result of a match operation. Contains query methods to determine match boundaries, groups, and captured text.
java.util.stream.Collectors: Implementations of Collector for reduction operations on streams. Provides methods for accumulating elements into collections, grouping, partitioning, and summarizing.
java.util.stream.Collectors.toList: Returns a Collector that accumulates input elements into a new List. No guarantees on mutability, serializability, or thread-safety of the returned List.
java.io.File: An abstract representation of file and directory pathnames. Provides methods for file/directory creation, deletion, and attribute access.
java.io.File.createTempFile: Creates an empty file in the default or specified directory with a generated unique name using the given prefix and suffix.
java.io.File.pathSeparator: The system-dependent path-separator character as a string. Used to separate filenames in path lists (':' on Unix, ';' on Windows).
java.io.InputStream: Abstract superclass of all classes representing an input stream of bytes. Subclasses must implement read() to provide the next byte.
java.io.OutputStream: Abstract superclass of all classes representing an output stream of bytes. Subclasses must implement write(int) to accept output bytes.
java.io.Writer: Abstract class for writing to character streams. Subclasses must implement write(char[], int, int), flush(), and close().
java.io.BufferedWriter: Writes text to a character-output stream, buffering characters for efficient writing. Provides a platform-aware newLine() method.
java.io.FileWriter: Writes text to character files using a default buffer size. Encoding uses specified charset or platform default.
java.io.PrintWriter: Prints formatted representations of objects to a text-output stream. Supports automatic flushing and never throws IOExceptions directly.
java.io.StringWriter: A character stream that collects output in a string buffer, which can then be used to construct a string. Closing has no effect.
java.io.DataOutput: Interface for converting Java primitive types to bytes and writing them to a binary stream. Also supports modified UTF-8 string writing.
java.nio.ByteBuffer: A buffer for byte data with support for both heap and direct allocation. Provides methods for reading/writing primitives with configurable byte order.
java.nio.CharBuffer: A buffer for character data. Implements CharSequence for compatibility with regex and other APIs. Supports bulk transfer operations.
java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets: Defines constants for standard charsets guaranteed on all Java implementations: US_ASCII, ISO_8859_1, UTF_8, UTF_16, UTF_16BE, UTF_16LE.
java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8: Eight-bit Unicode Transformation Format. The most commonly used encoding for text data.
java.net.URI: Represents a Uniform Resource Identifier reference per RFC 2396. Provides parsing, construction, and manipulation of URI components.
java.net.URL: Represents a Uniform Resource Locator pointing to a resource on the Web. Provides methods to open connections and retrieve content.
javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest: Extends ServletRequest to provide request information for HTTP servlets. Provides methods to access HTTP headers, cookies, session, and request parameters.
javax.servlet.http.HttpSession: Provides a way to identify a user across multiple page requests and store information about that user. Sessions are maintained on the server.
javax.swing.JScrollPane: A scrollable view of a lightweight component. Provides scroll bars to navigate content that is larger than the visible area.
javax.swing.JTable: A component for displaying and editing regular two-dimensional tables of cells. Supports sorting, filtering, and custom cell rendering.
javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeLater: Causes the Runnable to be executed asynchronously on the AWT event dispatching thread. Used to safely update the UI from background threads.
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils: Operations on String that are null safe. Provides utility methods for string manipulation including checks, transformations, and parsing.
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.sub: Gets the substring after the last occurrence of a separator. Returns an empty string if nothing is found.
org.joda.time.DateTime: An immutable representation of date and time with timezone. Part of Joda-Time library, predecessor to java.time API.
org.joda.time.Days: An immutable time period representing a number of days. Provides methods for date arithmetic and comparison.
org.joda.time.Days.getDays: Returns the number of days in this Days period.
com.google.gson.JsonObject: A class representing a JSON object. Provides methods to add, get, and manipulate JSON properties. Part of Google's Gson library.
com.alibaba.fastjson2.JSONObject.NONE_DI: A constant in Alibaba's FastJSON2 library representing a feature set for JSON processing configuration.
io.protostuff.StringSerializer.STRING: A serializer for String types in the Protostuff serialization library.
io.protostuff.StringSerializer.STRING.de: Deserializer method for String types in the Protostuff serialization library.
io.protostuff.WireFormat.TAG_TYPE_BITS: The number of bits used to represent the tag type in Protocol Buffers wire format.
io.protostuff.WireFormat.WIRETYPE_LENGTH: Wire type constant indicating a length-delimited value (strings, bytes, embedded messages) in Protocol Buffers format.
org.apache.skywalking.apm.network.langua: Represents a thread snapshot for profiling in Apache SkyWalking APM (Application Performance Monitoring).
Parses a ThreadSnapshot from a delimited input stream using Protocol Buffers format.
org.atmosphere.cpr.AtmosphereResourceImp: A constant used in Atmosphere framework for WebSocket/Comet communication.
org.atmosphere.cpr.BroadcastFilter.Broad: Represents an action to be taken during broadcast filtering in the Atmosphere framework.
A constant indicating that the broadcast should be aborted.
